text.title: Sample lesson: how two sides heard one signing
text.question: When both sides signed, did they agree on what the signing meant?
text.goal: Compare what Ottawa sought from the numbered treaties with what First Nations understood signing to mean.
text.prior: Lessons 5–6: early treaties, the Royal Proclamation, and Confederation.
text.h2: Two purposes meet at the signing table
text.p1: Ottawa sent commissioners west with written instructions: secure land for settlement and a railway, at the lowest cost the Crown could defend. The commissioners carried printed treaty terms and the authority to promise reserves, schools, and annuities.
text.p2: First Nations leaders heard the same meetings through ceremony and oral record. Promises spoken at the table carried the weight of the agreement, whether or not a clerk wrote them into the printed text.
text.sourceExtract: The Indians asked for many things, and we promised what the written terms allowed; what they carried home was what they heard spoken.
text.sourceLimits: A Crown record only; it cannot speak for what First Nations understood.
text.workedStep: Name one thing each side wanted before you compare the signing.
text.workedResponse: Ottawa wanted secure land at low cost; First Nations wanted a relationship the spoken promises described.
text.supportedTask: Use the same two-column comparison on the second sample passage.
text.supportedFeedback: A strong answer names one purpose per side and cites the passage.
text.independentTask: Compare the two purposes using the third sample passage as your evidence.
text.independentCriteria: Names one purpose per side; cites the passage; states the difference in one sentence.
